experiences.title: Into The Wild
experiences.summary: A hands-on wilderness workshop in Sainj Valley where participants spend 4 nights and 5 days living with minimal excess while learning mountain survival, camp systems, teamwork, and Leave No Trace habits.
exclusions: Travel to/from pickup point unless specified
itinerary: Day 1: Pickup from Aut, arrival at KEAS base, safety briefing, gear check, camp discipline, and introduction to low-impact wilderness living.
Day 2: Shelter building, knot practice, tarp systems, fire-making methods, stove safety, and evening reflection around decision-making in the wild.
Day 3: Water sourcing, filtration and purification, emergency signalling, basic wilderness first aid, and team problem-solving drills.
Day 4: Jungle navigation, river-crossing basics, route choice, leadership rotation, Leave No Trace field practice, and a guided survival scenario.
Day 5: Final scenario debrief, personal preparedness plan, certificate/closing circle, pack-out audit, and drop at Aut.

experiences.title: The Art of Navigation
experiences.location: Sainj Valley forest, meadow terrain, and open alpine areas
experiences.summary: A map, compass, and route-planning course built for beginners and improving trekkers who want real confidence reading terrain, following bearings, estimating time, and navigating without depending only on phone signal.
itinerary: Day 1: Pickup from Aut, Sainj orientation, map symbols, scale, contour lines, route-risk briefing, and field notebook setup.
Day 2: Compass handling, bearings, back-bearings, pacing, timing, handrails, catching features, and short relocation drills near base.
Day 3: Follow bearings through mixed forest and meadow terrain, identify prominent terrain features, and review route choices in pairs.
Day 4: Build a safe route plan using map, compass, GPS, and smartphone cross-checks; estimate distance, height gain, and travel time.
Day 5: Team-led navigation exercise over forest and open terrain with instructor observation, emergency scenarios, and decision reviews.
Day 6: Final route-planning assessment, debrief, individual improvement notes, certificate/closing circle, and drop at Aut.

experiences.title: Buran Pass Trek
experiences.summary: A post-monsoon crossover trek from the Shimla side toward Kinnaur, combining old villages, forests, Dayara meadows, Chandranahan-side acclimatization, a high pass crossing, and a dramatic descent toward Barua.
inclusions: Camping or local stay as per route
exclusions: Porter/mule for personal bag unless booked
itinerary: Day 1: Pickup from Shimla and drive toward Janglik. Check documents, settle into the stay, review weather, gear, layering, and the route plan.
Day 2: Trek from Janglik through village paths, forest sections, and open meadows toward Dayara. Focus on easy pacing and hydration.
Day 3: Move from Dayara toward Litham through rolling meadows and stream sections. Use the day to acclimatize and prepare for higher camps.
Day 4: Acclimatization and exploration day around the Chandranahan side, then return/rest near Litham as per weather and team condition.
Day 5: Trek from Litham toward Dunda high camp. Review pass-day timing, snow/terrain conditions, and early-rest protocol.
Day 6: Cross Buran Pass with controlled pacing and leader-managed descent. Continue toward Munirang / Barua-side camp depending on conditions.
Day 7: Trek/drive out via Barua side and return transfer toward Shimla. Final debrief, buffer handling, and drop as per road conditions.
experiences.startEnd: Shimla - Janglik - Buran Pass - Barua - Shimla

experiences.title: Raktisar Trek
experiences.location: Great Himalayan National Park core zone
experiences.summary: A longer GHNP core-zone trek toward Raktisar, shaped around the KEAS base route noted at roughly 70 km with remote camps, forest-to-alpine transitions, permit-aware movement, and slower pacing for a small six-person team.
itinerary: Day 1: Pickup from Aut, arrival at KEAS base, permit and safety briefing, medical disclosure, gear audit, and route overview.
Day 2: Begin the approach from KEAS base into forested Sainj Valley trails. Practice steady pacing, hydration discipline, and camp routines.
Day 3: Continue through GHNP valley terrain toward remote camp. Expect forest, stream sections, and a clear Leave No Trace campsite system.
Day 4: Gain altitude gradually through mixed forest and meadow terrain. Review weather, route options, and team health before upper camps.
Day 5: Move toward higher alpine approach terrain with slower pacing, terrain-awareness drills, and early rest for the objective section.
Day 6: Raktisar / Rakti Sar objective day as permitted by weather, trail, and team condition. Explore the high basin and return to camp safely.
Day 7: Begin the return route with campsite clean-up, waste audit, and careful descent through alpine-to-meadow sections.
Day 8: Descend through forest and river-valley terrain, using recovery pacing and local ecology interpretation through the day.
Day 9: Trek back toward KEAS base, close the field loop, dry gear, debrief decisions, and celebrate the team finish.
Day 10: Breakfast, contingency wrap-up, feedback circle, and drop at Aut.

expeditions.title: Friendship Peak
expeditions.summary: A Manali-side snow objective for fit trekkers ready to progress into crampon movement, rope-team discipline, snow-slope judgement, and a guided summit attempt.
itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Manali, equipment audit, medical screening, and expedition briefing.
Day 2: Acclimatization hike toward Solang / Patalsu side and snow craft orientation.
Day 3: Trek to approach camp via Dhundi and Bakarthach meadows.
Day 4: Move to Lady Leg / advance base; crampon, ice axe, and rope-team practice.
Day 5: Summit attempt on Friendship Peak and return to base camp.
Day 6: Reserve weather day for summit or recovery.
Day 7: Descend to roadhead, debrief, certificate, and depart Manali.

expeditions.title: Pin Bhaba Pass
expeditions.summary: A dramatic crossover from the green Bhaba Valley to the stark Pin Valley, built around Kafnu approach days, meadow camps, moraine travel, pass-day pacing, and the exit to Mudh.
itinerary: Day 1: Shimla / Rampur transfer to Kafnu, permits, briefing, and gear check.
Day 2: Trek Kafnu to Mulling through forest, river sections, and meadow camps.
Day 3: Mulling to Kara with gradual altitude gain and stream crossings.
Day 4: Kara to Phustirang, pass briefing, early dinner, and weather review.
Day 5: Cross Pin Bhaba Pass and descend toward Mangrungse / Baldar terrain.
Day 6: Trek to Mudh village in Pin Valley and transfer toward Kaza.
Day 7: Buffer / road contingency day for weather, roadblocks, or acclimatization.

expeditions.title: Hanuman Tibba
expeditions.summary: A serious pyramid-shaped alpine objective north-west of Manali, suitable only for trained climbers with snow, ice, rope, camp discipline, and altitude experience.
itinerary: Day 1: Arrive Manali, document check, medical screen, and technical gear issue.
Day 2: Skills refresh: knots, fixed rope movement, cramponing, and crevasse response.
Day 3: Drive to Solang / Dhundi and trek toward Beas Kund base zone.
Day 4: Establish base camp, acclimatization walk, and load planning.
Day 5: Ferry load to Camp 1 and return for recovery.
Day 6: Move to Camp 1; snow anchors and route condition assessment.
Day 7: Establish higher camp depending on snow and weather.
Day 8: Summit attempt with alpine start and descent to lower camp.
Day 9: Reserve summit / weather day.
Day 10: Descend to base camp and clear route loads.
Day 11: Trek out to roadhead and transfer to Manali for debrief.

expeditions.title: Deo Tibba
expeditions.summary: A 6,001 m snow-dome objective above Jagatsukh that demands glacier travel, moraine negotiation, load-ferry planning, fixed-line judgement, and strong acclimatization.
packing: Harness and technical hardware as advised

journalPosts.title: Why Sainj Valley works for slower, deeper adventure
journalPosts.excerpt: Sainj rewards travellers who want forests, village rhythm, GHNP ecozone access, and enough quiet to actually notice the landscape.
body: Sainj Valley is not designed for rushed checklist travel. That is exactly why it works for KEAS programs. The valley gives groups access to forest trails, village stays, rock craft, food systems, and slower conversations around ecology.

The operating advantage is rhythm. Groups can move in the morning, pause through the day, and use evenings for debrief, recovery, or community time. That makes Sainj especially strong for schools, creator retreats, WFH cohorts, and low-impact adventure programs.
KEAS treats Sainj as a base for learning and decompression rather than a backdrop. The route, stay, activity level, and cultural touchpoints are matched to the group.

journalPosts.title: How KEAS builds safety briefings into every route
journalPosts.excerpt: Good safety is not a paragraph in a brochure. It is a repeated habit before, during, and after every mountain day.
body: Every KEAS route starts with expectation-setting. We look at fitness, prior experience, weather, terrain, gear, road conditions, and the purpose of the group before finalising the day plan.

In the field, safety is communicated in simple language: what the terrain asks of you, where the hazards are, how the group will move, and what changes if conditions shift. This is especially important for rock craft, high passes, and expedition approaches.
Post-activity debriefs help guests understand their own decision-making, recovery needs, hydration, and readiness for the next day.

journalPosts.title: Designing Himalayan workations that still feel like travel
journalPosts.excerpt: A good workation protects work hours and travel energy. The trick is not doing everything; it is designing the day well.
body: Most workations fail when the itinerary ignores work. KEAS designs these programs around predictable work blocks, morning movement, evening recovery, and realistic expectations around connectivity.

A good day may include a short forest walk, a rock craft session, or a village experience before work begins. The afternoon stays protected, while evenings are used for decompression, food, or community time.
The goal is not to squeeze a vacation around calls. It is to create a mountain rhythm that lets people work clearly and still return home with a real sense of place.
